title: Unified Firebase app: user schema alignment, global header/profile menu, and in-app admin dashboard

requirements.summary: Align Firestore `users/{uid}` document shape to the required fields and ensure signup + profile reads use that schema.
acceptanceCriteria: After signup, the Firestore document at `users/{uid}` exists and contains `name`, `email`, `photoURL`, `role`, `approved`, and `createdAt` (as a Firestore Timestamp, e.g., via `serverTimestamp()`), with no dependency on additional required fields.
Login gating continues to rely on the boolean `approved === true` from a fresh server read.
The app can display the logged-in user’s `name`, `role`, and `photoURL` using the new schema.

file_operations.description: Update `UserProfile`/related types to match exactly the required schema fields: `name`, `email`, `photoURL`, `role`, `approved`, `createdAt` (Firestore timestamp type), and remove/stop relying on any extra profile fields for required app flows.

Update Firestore write/read helpers to (1) write ONLY the required fields into `users/{uid}` on signup using Firestore `serverTimestamp()` for `createdAt`, (2) map the existing processed profile image data URL into `photoURL`, and (3) update profile read helpers to return `name`, `role`, and `photoURL` (plus `approved`) from a fresh server read (no cache).

Adjust signup submission payload to match the required user schema (e.g., send `name` and `photoURL`), and ensure UI copy/errors remain in English while keeping existing image capture/processing behavior.

Update Home screen to display the logged-in user’s `name`, `role`, and `photoURL` from the new schema (avoid hardcoded placeholders for profile identity) and rely on the shared/global header for logout and identity display instead of its own header.

requirements.summary: Implement first-ever signup behavior: first user becomes `super_admin` and approved; later signups become unapproved `user`.
acceptanceCriteria: When the users collection is empty, the first signup creates `users/{uid}` with `role="super_admin"` and `approved=true`.
When at least one user exists, a new signup creates `users/{uid}` with `role="user"` and `approved=false`.

file_operations.description: Ensure the first-user check is used during profile creation to set `role`/`approved` per requirement (first signup => `super_admin`+approved, otherwise `user`+unapproved), and keep the decision fully derived from Firestore state before writing.
Update the smoke test checklist to explicitly verify the first-user `super_admin`+approved behavior vs subsequent `user`+unapproved behavior using the `users/{uid}` schema and fresh reads.

requirements.summary: Add a global header on all routes with app logo/name on the left and (when logged in) a clickable avatar on the right.
acceptanceCriteria: All routes/screens render the same header at the top of the viewport.
Header left renders an app logo image asset and an app name string.
When a user is logged in, the header right renders their `photoURL` as an avatar button; when logged out, the avatar area is hidden or replaced with a neutral placeholder (no errors).

file_operations.description: Create a global `AppHeader` component rendering left: logo image + app name; right: authenticated user avatar button using `photoURL`. Use shadcn-ui composition (e.g., Avatar/Button primitives) for consistent styling. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
Add a small hook that subscribes to Firebase Auth state (e.g., onAuthStateChanged via CDN-loaded module) and exposes current auth user (uid/email) for header visibility and profile loading.
Add a hook that fetches the current user's `users/{uid}` profile (fresh server read) and returns `name`, `role`, `photoURL`, `approved` for use across header, home, and admin guarding.

Wrap all routed screens with a shared layout that includes `AppHeader` at the top so it renders on every route; ensure the avatar area behaves safely when logged out. Wire the new hooks into the layout to drive authenticated header state.

requirements.summary: Implement header avatar profile popup showing name+role, conditional admin dashboard entry, and logout behavior back to `/login`.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking the avatar opens a popup/menu anchored to the avatar button.
Popup contains visible text for the user `name` and `role`.
For `role in {admin, super_admin}`, popup shows a button labeled exactly "Open Admin Dashboard" that navigates to the admin area.
Popup always includes a "Logout" button that signs out and navigates to `/login`.

file_operations.description: Create a `ProfileMenu` component anchored to the header avatar that shows the user's name + role, conditionally renders a button labeled exactly "Open Admin Dashboard" for `admin`/`super_admin`, and always renders a "Logout" action. Use shadcn-ui Dropdown Menu primitives for the popup behavior. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
Integrate `ProfileMenu` into the avatar area so clicking the avatar opens the anchored menu and displays `name` + `role`.
Ensure there is a single sign-out helper used by the profile menu logout action; on logout, clear any cached in-memory UI state as needed and allow navigation to `/login` without errors.
Add navigation wiring so profile-menu logout reliably navigates to `/login`, and "Open Admin Dashboard" navigates to the admin area route(s) within the same SPA.

requirements.summary: Add an in-app Admin Dashboard (same SPA) with role-guarded access and 5 sections: Dashboard, Users, Chats, Reports, Settings.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigating to an admin route while not `admin`/`super_admin` redirects back to the non-admin area (e.g., `/home`) and does not render admin content.
Admin Dashboard includes navigation to the 5 required pages/sections within the same SPA.
Dashboard page shows basic stats placeholders derived from Firestore where feasible (e.g., total users, approved users, pending users).
Chats/Reports/Settings pages can be UI placeholders but must exist and be reachable via the admin navigation.

file_operations.description: Create an `AdminLayout` that provides responsive admin navigation (mobile-friendly) and a content outlet area for the 5 sections. Use shadcn-ui composition (e.g., Tabs/Sheet/Buttons) to support a WhatsApp-style clean UI. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
Create the Admin Dashboard (stats) screen and display basic Firestore-derived counts (e.g., total users, approved users, pending users) with safe loading/error states.
Create the Admin Users list screen entry (table/list shell) and wire it into the admin navigation (full management actions implemented under REQ-6).
Create a reachable Chats screen as a UI placeholder (no realtime chat implementation).
Create a reachable Reports screen as a UI placeholder.
Create a reachable Settings screen as a UI placeholder.
Extend SPA routing to include admin routes for Dashboard/Users/Chats/Reports/Settings, and wire route navigation links/buttons from the profile menu and admin layout.
Add an admin-only guard wrapper that uses a fresh Firestore role read (`admin`/`super_admin`) to allow rendering admin routes, otherwise redirects to `/home` without rendering admin content.

requirements.summary: Implement Admin Dashboard Users list with Firestore-backed listing and role-based management actions (approve/block and role changes), including super_admin visibility and protections.
acceptanceCriteria: Users list shows all users in the `users` collection (admins and super_admins included).
Approve action updates the selected user document such that they can log in (i.e., `approved` becomes `true`).
Block action updates the selected user such that they cannot log in anymore (e.g., `approved` becomes `false`), and the UI reflects the blocked/unapproved state.
Role change action allows toggling `role` between `user` and `admin` for non-super_admin users according to the current operator’s permissions.
The UI prevents changing any user to `super_admin` via the dashboard and prevents demoting a `super_admin` user via the dashboard.

file_operations.description: Add Firestore helpers to (1) list all `users` documents, and (2) update `approved` and `role` fields for a target user (using appropriate Firestore update operations), while keeping all writes constrained to the required schema fields.

Implement the users list UI by fetching all `users` docs and rendering each user's name/email/role/approved state and avatar (via `photoURL`). Add action controls to approve/block and to toggle role user↔admin. Enforce UI permission rules: never allow setting `super_admin`, never allow demoting/changing a `super_admin` unless operator is `super_admin`, and ensure `super_admin` users still appear in the list.
Add a hook to load the full users collection for admin listing (with loading/error states) and expose a refetch method after admin actions.

Create a composed action-control component for each user row/card (approve/block and role toggle), enforcing the operator-permission constraints in the UI. Use shadcn-ui composition (e.g., Dropdown Menu, Alert Dialog, Buttons) for consistent interactions. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Update Firestore security rules to enforce role-based permissions for user listing and management and prevent client writes to `super_admin` except where unavoidable.
acceptanceCriteria: A non-admin authenticated user can read only `users/{auth.uid}` and cannot update `role` or `approved`.
An admin/super_admin can read all documents in `users` (required for the user list).
Client writes that attempt to create/update any document with `role == "super_admin"` are denied by Firestore rules (except for the first-user creation flow if supported by current rule strategy).
Updates to an existing `super_admin` user’s `role`/`approved` are rejected unless the requester is `super_admin`.

file_operations.description: Tighten rules to: (1) keep non-admin users limited to reading their own `users/{uid}` and disallow changing `role`/`approved`; (2) allow admins/super_admins to read all users; (3) deny updates that set `role` to `super_admin`; (4) restrict updates to an existing `super_admin` user's `role`/`approved` to only requests made by a `super_admin` requester (while still allowing listing visibility).

Update deployment/runbook notes to include validating the updated Firestore rules for admin listing and user management actions (approve/block/role changes) and verifying the `super_admin` protection constraints.

requirements.summary: Apply a clean, WhatsApp-style, mobile-friendly UI with a green-forward palette and consistent English text across auth, header, home, and admin.
acceptanceCriteria: Primary navigation and key actions are easily usable on mobile widths (~360px) without horizontal scrolling.
Admin Dashboard navigation is usable on mobile (e.g., collapsible sidebar, tabs, or a responsive drawer).
All visible UI strings are in English.
Visual styling is consistent across screens and matches a simple WhatsApp-like aesthetic.

file_operations.description: Refine global styling tokens (spacing/typography defaults and green-forward color emphasis) to keep a consistent WhatsApp-like aesthetic across screens while avoiding blue/purple primary accents.
If needed, adjust Tailwind theme extensions to better support the green-forward palette and consistent typography across header, auth, home, and admin UI.
Align auth layout spacing and visual hierarchy with the unified WhatsApp-style design and ensure all user-facing strings remain English (no stray placeholder branding).

Ensure admin navigation is responsive on mobile (e.g., drawer/sheet or tabbed navigation), with consistent spacing and readable touch targets. Use shadcn-ui composition where applicable. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Add a static generated app logo asset and render it in the global header.
acceptanceCriteria: A logo file exists under `frontend/public/assets/generated/` and is used in the header.
Logo renders crisply at typical header sizes (~24–32px) on light and dark backgrounds.

file_operations.description: Add the generated logo asset file at exactly `frontend/public/assets/generated/app-logo.dim_256x256.png` and keep it optimized for crisp rendering at ~24–32px in the header.

Render the static logo asset from `frontend/public/assets/generated/app-logo.dim_256x256.png` next to the app name on the left side of the global header, sized appropriately for a compact WhatsApp-style header.
